citation.title: Time series extrinsic regression for reconstructing missing electron temperature in tokamak
citation.authors: Wang M, Wan C, Lu J, Yu Z, Xiao B, Li Y, He X, Luo Z, Yuan Q, Hu Y, Li J
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/1741-4326/addb5f (this paper's own DOI, PDF p2 header; reference-list DOIs belong to cited works)

scope_read.limitations: Figures are read from extracted images. No code or data were inspected. The text in Sec 2.2 lists 14 inputs and omits Li, while Table 1 lists 15. Line of sight is given as R=1.85 m but the target as R=1.9 m. The quoted loss is 0.014 (p8 Sec 2.3) versus test MSE 0.17 (p9 Table 4), with normalization unstated.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The source estimator is offline or real-time.
claim_checks.source_finding: The estimator is offline. Inputs include offline-EFIT quantities, and the authors state that this dependence limits real-time deployment. No timing was reported.
claim_checks.locator: p5 Sec 2.2 and Fig 1b; p10 Sec 4
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: On EAST, a transformer-plus-recurrent extrinsic regression model reconstructed single-radius ECE electron temperature over whole discharges from magnetic, interferometer and offline-EFIT signals, as an offline gap-filling tool.
claim_checks.qualification: The sentence describes an offline reconstruction, not a demonstrated deployment.

claim_checks.source_finding: The model uses a bidirectional RNN described as integrating past and future time steps. It works on fixed-length windows that span the discharge and was compared against two-sided whole-sequence reconstruction. Te/ECE is the target, not an input.
claim_checks.locator: p4 Sec 2.1; p7 Sec 2.2; p9 Table 3 (Bidirectional=True) and Fig 3
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Such whole-window, bidirectional reconstruction addresses a different task from causal nowcasting of a current report from strictly past information.
claim_checks.qualification: Do not generalize this to other prior work.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The validation design and the stated confidence level.
claim_checks.source_finding: The data are 1873 discharges (#82827-#100000). The split is described as chronological 80/20 by discharge (p5), but also as random 10% validation and test subsets (p8). The test set is 374 shots spanning #82877-#99092. The target is Savitzky-Golay-smoothed ECE Te. The '95.9% confidence level' is a mean per-shot coverage fraction, stated as within 2σ in the abstract but within 1σ in Sec 3 and the Fig 5 caption, with σ undefined. Mean ∞-norm similarity is 86.5% (Fig 4). Test loss appears in the hyperparameter comparison.
claim_checks.locator: p2 Abstract; p5 Sec 2.2; p8 Sec 3; p9 Fig 3 and Table 4; p11 Figs 4-5
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: On a 374-shot test set, the authors report R² of 0.92 and mean per-shot coverage of about 96% within a standard-deviation band of the smoothed ECE target.
claim_checks.qualification: This is coverage, not a statistical confidence interval. The band width is ambiguous, the labels are smoothed ECE rather than physical truth, and the split description is internally inconsistent.

input_target_timing.inputs: 15 signals at about 1 kHz: Ip, Vloop, Bt0, line ne (HCN), Wmhd, βn, βp, βt, κ, Li, q0, q95, δt, δb (offline EFIT), and NBI/ECRH heating ratio
input_target_timing.outputs: Te at R≈1.9 m from 32-channel HRS ECE, downsampled to 1 kHz, smoothed (SG window 59, order 1), with cutoff periods masked
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: The target is a processed ECE-derived Te label, not independent truth. The claim to 'replace HRS' (p10 Sec 4) is an author claim.

validation.temporal_order: Ambiguous: described as chronological on p5 and random on p8
validation.unknowns: Exact shot assignment; σ definition; ∞-norm similarity formula; normalization; whether test loss influenced model selection beyond Fig 3; per-regime errors

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Nothing. Only parameter count (~36M) and training hardware are reported.
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Latency, real-time operation, uptime or cost benefits (these are author claims only)

forbidden_inferences: The source performs real-time or causal Te estimation
The 95.9% figure is a confidence interval or 2σ coverage
Validation on untouched or chronologically later data
Applicability to CES/ion or impurity temperature
Superiority claims transferable to our task
Mechanistic physics identified from Pearson/Granger analysis
competing_or_complementary: Complementary motivation: missing-diagnostic reconstruction framed as extrinsic regression from routine signals. It contrasts with our setting on causality (offline two-sided vs causal nowcast), quantity (ECE Te vs reported CES carbon temperature), and inputs (EFIT/global signals vs BES/ECEI voltages plus past CES reports). Its two-sided reconstruction resembles our interpolation reference, not our estimator.
